title: ux-review-plan.v1
description: S073. PROJECT-OWNED declaration of what a UX review must cover. This is the load-bearing half of the evidence contract: the expected fixture matrix comes from HERE, never from the reviewer's own output. A reviewer willing to skip the work is equally willing to write 'matrix: n=0,1,2,3' — so the reviewer reports only what it OBSERVED, and the validator computes expected minus observed. Lives at the project root (conventionally .ux-review.yaml or .ux-review.json) and is authored by the project, not by an agent mid-review.

viewports.description: Every surface is measured at every viewport unless it narrows the list. The incident shipped a 74px card-number field at 390px because mobile was never exercised.

hot_spot.description: Hot spots require the FULL fixture matrix. Everything else may use the reduced matrix. A requirement so heavy it is always waived is worthless, so cost is tiered deliberately rather than by omission.

viewport_ids.description: Narrow to a subset of the declared viewports. Absent = all of them.

fixtures.description: The collection-cardinality states this surface must be reviewed in. The generalised invariant behind 'cart with 0/1/2/3+ line items' — it applies equally to a search-results page, a dashboard table, or an empty inbox.

expected_cardinality.description: How many items the collection should hold in this state. The driver reports what it OBSERVED; a mismatch fails, because a fixture that did not actually materialise cannot support a verdict.

min_item_quantity.description: At least one item at this quantity (e.g. qty>=2). Quantity-dependent layout defects hide behind qty=1.

setup.description: How the state is reached. Replayed, never invented by the reviewer.

collection_selector.description: Selector whose match count IS the observed cardinality. Without it the count cannot be verified and the cell is UNVERIFIED, not passed.

required_capabilities.description: Integrations that must be PRESENT for this surface to be reviewable at all — e.g. a payment gateway. The incident's dev environment had no gateways installed, so the entire checkout payment block did not exist there and a full local pass returned clean on a surface that was not rendered. A missing capability makes the surface UNMEASURED, never PASS.

relations.description: Tier B declared relations. Optional — Tier A runs with no declaration at all.

severity_floor.description: Findings below this are recorded but do not fail the gate.

environment.description: What the review environment must satisfy. Recorded into evidence so a pass cannot be transplanted from a materially different environment.
